title: Smooth Cobordism Relations Groups and Rings

items.title: Unoriented smooth cobordism of closed manifolds
items.statement: Fix $n\ge0$. A (unoriented) bordism from a closed smooth $n$-manifold $M_0$ to a closed smooth $n$-manifold $M_1$ is data $(W,\theta_0,\theta_1)$ consisting of a compact smooth $(n+1)$-manifold $W$ with a decomposition $\partial W=(\partial W)_0\sqcup(\partial W)_1$ into open and closed boundary subsets, together with smooth embeddings $\theta_0:[0,1)\times M_0\to W$ and $\theta_1:(-1,0]\times M_1\to W$ onto open collar neighbourhoods of $(\partial W)_0$ and $(\partial W)_1$ with $\theta_i(\{0\}\times M_i)=(\partial W)_i$. Closed $n$-manifolds $M_0$ and $M_1$ are cobordant if such data exist. The collar embeddings are part of the data, so that gluing may use supplied collars rather than fresh choices. Empty manifolds and $n=0$ are included; 'closed' means compact without boundary.
items.strategy: Restate Freed's Definition 1.19 with collar embeddings included, fixing the boundary-part notation $(\partial W)_0,(\partial W)_1$ and the meaning of 'closed'. Record that only existence of the data is used for the relation, so reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity are argued from the given collars; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Oriented smooth cobordism
items.statement: Let $M_0,M_1$ be closed oriented smooth $n$-manifolds. An oriented bordism from $M_0$ to $M_1$ is a bordism $(W,\theta_0,\theta_1)$ from $M_0$ to $M_1$ together with an orientation of $W$ such that the induced boundary orientation (outward-normal-first, as fixed on the manifolds-with-boundary page) on $(\partial W)_0$ is the negative of the supplied orientation of $M_0$ and on $(\partial W)_1$ is the supplied orientation of $M_1$. Equivalently, in the collar parametrization the embeddings $\theta_0,\theta_1$ are orientation-preserving for the product orientations of $[0,1)\times M_0$ and $(-1,0]\times M_1$, the intervals carrying their standard orientations. Oriented manifolds are oriented cobordant when such data exist. The opposite orientation of a manifold is written $-M$; the empty manifold carries its unique orientation.
items.strategy: Fix the sign once through the outward-normal-first convention: the incoming face contributes $-M_0$ and the outgoing face $M_1$. Prove that the boundary-orientation formulation and the orientation-preserving-collar formulation agree by computing the product orientation of $[0,1)\times M_0$ at $\{0\}\times M_0$ against the induced boundary orientation. Record that orientation reversal acts pointwise on determinant rays, so $-M$ is well defined.

items.title: Cylinders give reflexivity of cobordism
items.statement:
For every closed smooth $n$-manifold $M$, the product $M\times[0,1]$ with its
product smooth structure and the collars
$$\theta_0:[0,1)\times M\to M\times[0,1],\quad \theta_0(s,x)=(x,s),$$
$$\theta_1:(-1,0]\times M\to M\times[0,1],\quad \theta_1(s,x)=(x,1+s),$$
is a bordism from $M$ to $M$: take
$(\partial(M\times[0,1]))_0=M\times\{0\}$ and
$(\partial(M\times[0,1]))_1=M\times\{1\}$
([[def-unoriented-smooth-cobordism-of-closed-manifolds]]).

If $(M,o)$ is oriented and $[0,1]$ carries its standard orientation, then with
the product orientation $o\otimes dt$ of $M\times[0,1]$ the induced boundary
orientation ([[def-induced-boundary-orientation]]) on $M\times\{0\}$ is
$(-1)^{n+1}o$ and that on $M\times\{1\}$ is $(-1)^n o$; consequently
$M\times[0,1]$ oriented by $(-1)^n(o\otimes dt)$ is an oriented bordism from
$(M,o)$ to $(M,o)$ ([[def-oriented-smooth-cobordism]]). Hence $M$ is cobordant
to itself in both theories.
items.strategy: Construct the cylinder explicitly, identify its boundary and collars, and compute the two boundary orientations with the product-orientation rule (moving the outward normal past the $n$ tangent directions of the positive factor). The unoriented case is included. No choice is used.

items.title: Reversing a cobordism gives symmetry
items.statement: If $(W,\theta_0,\theta_1)$ is a bordism from $M_0$ to $M_1$, then swapping the two boundary parts and the two collar parametrizations yields a bordism from $M_1$ to $M_0$. In the oriented theory, if $W$ is an oriented bordism from $M_0$ to $M_1$, then the same manifold with the opposite orientation, again with the two boundary parts and collars interchanged, is an oriented bordism from $M_1$ to $M_0$: the induced boundary orientations match $-M_1$ on the incoming face and $M_0$ on the outgoing face.
items.strategy: Give the dual bordism of Freed (Definition 1.22) in the unoriented case and its orientation-reversed form in the oriented case; recompute the boundary signs from outward-normal-first and check that the reversed orientation makes the swapped collars orientation-preserving. No choice is used.

items.title: Collar gluing and seam smoothing give transitivity
items.statement:
Let $(W_1,\theta_0,\theta_1)$ be a bordism from a closed smooth $n$-manifold
$M_0$ to a closed smooth $n$-manifold $M_1$, and let
$(W_2,\theta'_0,\theta'_1)$ be a bordism from $M_1$ to a closed smooth
$n$-manifold $M_2$, with the same $M_1$ in both
([[def-unoriented-smooth-cobordism-of-closed-manifolds]]). The outgoing collar
$\theta_1:(-1,0]\times M_1\to W_1$ of the first and the incoming collar
$\theta'_0:[0,1)\times M_1\to W_2$ of the second agree on $M_1\times\{0\}$ after the seam identification and
combine to a bi-collar $M_1\times(-1,1)\to W_1\cup_{M_1}W_2$; thereby they
define a smooth structure on the glued space $W=W_1\cup_{M_1}W_2$ making it a
compact smooth $(n+1)$-manifold with boundary whose seam $M_1$ is interior.
The structure is canonical for the given data: it is the maximal atlas
generated by the two given smooth structures and the bi-collar, and, assuming $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), a change of
collar presentation changes it at most by a diffeomorphism fixed off a
neighbourhood of the seam, by the collar-comparison argument in
[[thm-the-double-has-a-well-defined-smooth-structure]]. The boundary
decomposes as $M_0\sqcup M_2$, and the outer collars $\theta_0$ and
$\theta'_1$ make $W$ a bordism from $M_0$ to $M_2$.

In the oriented theory, if both bordisms are oriented
([[def-oriented-smooth-cobordism]]), the induced orientations on the common
boundary component are opposite, the orientations glue to an orientation of
$W$, and with that orientation $W$ is an oriented bordism from $M_0$ to $M_2$.
The glued bordism and transitivity use only the supplied collars and require
no choice principle. The additional comparison of different collar systems
uses $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through the cited comparison theorem.
items.strategy: Build the bi-collar chart for the glued space from the given collar embeddings, verify compatibility of the two half-atlases across the seam, and check that the seam becomes interior. Identify the outer boundary faces and their induced orientations, and verify the orientation gluing using the opposite induced orientations on the common component; cite the published double construction as the model for seam smoothing.

items.title: Smooth cobordism is an equivalence relation
items.statement:
For every $n\ge0$, unoriented cobordism of closed smooth $n$-manifolds
([[def-unoriented-smooth-cobordism-of-closed-manifolds]]) and oriented
cobordism of closed oriented smooth $n$-manifolds
([[def-oriented-smooth-cobordism]]) are reflexive by cylinders, symmetric by
dual bordisms (orientation-reversed in the oriented case), and transitive by
collar gluing. Restricted to any set $S$ of such manifolds in either theory,
cobordism is therefore an equivalence relation
([[def-equivalence-relation]]) and partitions $S$ into classes $[M]_S$.
The collection of manifolds on arbitrary underlying sets is not itself a set;
global bordism sets and the notation $[M]$ use the bounded models introduced
in the subsequent bordism-group definition. No choice principle is used,
and no claim about diffeomorphism classification is made.
items.strategy: Assemble the three lemmas and discharge the axioms of an equivalence relation; keep the two theories parallel and make no claim about diffeomorphism classification. No choice is used.

items.title: Null-cobordant closed manifolds
items.statement: A closed smooth $n$-manifold $M$ is null-cobordant if it is cobordant to the empty manifold; equivalently there is a bordism $W$ with $(\partial W)_1=\emptyset$ and $(\partial W)_0$ identified with $M$, so that $M$ is the entire boundary of a compact $(n+1)$-manifold $W$ carrying a collar of all of $\partial W$. In the oriented theory $M$ is null-cobordant if it is oriented cobordant to the empty oriented manifold; because the incoming face contributes the negative orientation, this says that $M$ occurs as the orientation opposite to the induced boundary of some compact oriented $W$, and reversing the orientation of $W$ presents $M$ as an induced boundary. The empty manifold is null-cobordant, and null-cobordism depends only on the cobordism class.
items.strategy: Specialize the bordism definition to the empty outgoing boundary and translate between 'cobordant to empty' and 'is the whole boundary', keeping the orientation sign explicit and noting that it is absorbed by reversing $W$. No choice is used.

items.title: Unoriented and oriented bordism groups
items.statement:
Fix $n\ge0$. By the cobordism equivalence relation
([[thm-smooth-cobordism-is-an-equivalence-relation]]) the closed smooth
$n$-manifolds are partitioned into cobordism classes
([[def-unoriented-smooth-cobordism-of-closed-manifolds]]). Let
$$\Omega_n^{O}:=\{\,[M]\;:\;M\ \text{a closed smooth }n\text{-manifold}\,\}$$
be the set of these classes in the bounded model convention below, and let
$$\Omega_n^{SO}:=\{\,[Q,o]\;:\;(Q,o)\ \text{a closed oriented smooth }n\text{-manifold}\,\}$$
be the set of oriented cobordism classes
([[def-oriented-smooth-cobordism]]).

**Set-size convention.** For each $n$ use the set of all closed smooth
$n$-manifold structures on subsets of $U_n=\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb N$,
and in the oriented theory include the orientation datum, before taking the
quotient by cobordism. Every closed smooth $n$-manifold has such a model:
compactness gives a finite chart cover $(V_j,\varphi_j)_{j<k}$, and the map
$x\mapsto(\varphi_j(x),j)$, with $j$ the least index for which $x\in V_j$,
is injective into $U_n$. Transport the topology, maximal atlas, and supplied
orientation along this injection; its image is diffeomorphic to the original
manifold. This uses only a finite chart cover, not a choice of a model for every
manifold simultaneously. Two transported models are diffeomorphic, and a
cylinder of [[lem-cylinders-give-reflexivity-of-cobordism]] with outgoing
collar composed with a diffeomorphism's inverse shows they are cobordant (orientation-preservingly in the oriented case). Thus $[M]$
means the unique class of any such model. Products and disjoint unions are
returned to this set of models in the same way; their class is independent of
the transport.

**The operation.** Disjoint union of manifolds defines operations
$$[M]+[N]:=[M\sqcup N]\quad\text{on }\Omega_n^{O},\qquad [Q,o]+[R,p]:=[Q\sqcup R,\,o\sqcup p]\quad\text{on }\Omega_n^{SO},$$
where $o\sqcup p$ is the orientation of the disjoint union whose restriction to
each summand is the given orientation, and finite disjoint unions carry the transported component atlases
([[prop-countable-disjoint-unions-of-fixed-dimensional-smooth-manifolds-are-smooth-manifolds]]);
for summands with boundary the same construction uses half-space charts.
Finite union preserves compactness and combines finitely many countable bases,
so this boundary extension requires no countable choice.
The class of the empty $n$-manifold is the displayed **zero** $0$: it is
null-cobordant and is a two-sided identity for the operation, since
$M\sqcup\varnothing$ is canonically diffeomorphic to $M$
([[def-null-cobordant-closed-manifold]]).

**Well-definedness.** The operations are independent of the chosen
representatives. If $W_i$ is a bordism from $M_i$ to $M_i'$ for $i=0,1$, then
the disjoint union $W_0\sqcup W_1$ carries the canonical smooth structure of a
compact $(n+1)$-manifold with boundary
$\partial(W_0\sqcup W_1)=(\partial W_0)\sqcup(\partial W_1)$, the collars
$\theta_0^0\sqcup\theta_0^1$ and $\theta_1^0\sqcup\theta_1^1$ are smooth
embeddings onto collar neighbourhoods of the boundary parts, and the
decomposition of the boundary into the two parts is again open and closed;
hence $W_0\sqcup W_1$ is a bordism from $M_0\sqcup M_1$ to
$M_0'\sqcup M_1'$. In the oriented case, orienting the disjoint union by the
given orientations makes the disjoint union of the oriented bordisms an
oriented bordism between the disjoint unions, because the induced boundary
orientation is computed componentwise and each summand carries its required
sign. Thus $[M_0\sqcup M_1]=[M_0'\sqcup M_1']$ whenever $[M_i]=[M_i']$, and
similarly in the oriented theory. The class of a finite disjoint union is
computed from the canonical smooth structure on disjoint unions; no further
choice is made.

**Deferred axioms and the forgetful map.** That these operations satisfy the
group axioms (associativity, commutativity, identity and inverses) is not
asserted here: it is proved in the following theorem, together with the
finiteness of the inverse in the unoriented theory. The **forgetful map**
$$\Omega_n^{SO}\longrightarrow\Omega_n^{O},\qquad [Q,o]\longmapsto[Q],$$
sends the oriented class of a closed oriented $n$-manifold to its underlying
unoriented cobordism class; it is well defined because an oriented bordism
between two oriented manifolds is in particular a bordism between their
underlying manifolds, so oriented cobordant manifolds are cobordant.
items.strategy: Define the two sets of classes using the equivalence-relation theorem, define the operation by disjoint union, and state the empty class; defer all axioms to the following theorem rather than asserting them here. Use the published smooth-structure result for finite disjoint unions; no smooth structure is chosen afresh.

items.title: Disjoint union makes bordism classes abelian groups
items.statement:
For each $n\ge0$, the operations $[M]+[N]=[M\sqcup N]$ and
$[Q,o]+[R,p]=[Q\sqcup R,o\sqcup p]$ make $(\Omega_n^{O},+)$ and
$(\Omega_n^{SO},+)$ abelian groups
([[def-unoriented-and-oriented-bordism-groups]], [[def-group]]). The operation
is well defined: if $M_i$ is cobordant to $M_i'$ for $i=0,1$, the disjoint
unions $M_0\sqcup M_1$ and $M_0'\sqcup M_1'$ are cobordant via the disjoint
union of the two bordisms. It is associative and commutative, the canonical
diffeomorphisms of finite disjoint unions identifying the two bracketings and
the two orders, and the class of the empty manifold is a two-sided identity.
Inverses: for every closed $M$, $[M]+[M]=0$ in $\Omega_n^{O}$ because
$M\sqcup M$ is the boundary of $M\times[0,1]$; for every closed oriented
$(M,o)$, $[M,o]+[-M]=0$ in $\Omega_n^{SO}$ because $M\sqcup(-M)$ is the
boundary of the cylinder with the appropriate orientation. No choice principle
is used.
items.strategy: Prove well-definedness from disjoint unions of bordisms; obtain associativity and commutativity from the canonical diffeomorphisms of finite disjoint unions; use the cylinder $M\times[0,1]$ with its two boundary signs to produce the inverse in each theory, computing the oriented boundary as $M\sqcup(-M)$. Cite the published smooth structure on finite disjoint unions.

items.title: The fundamental class of a boundary pushes forward to zero
items.statement: Let $W$ be a compact $R$-oriented $(n+1)$-manifold with boundary $M=\partial W$, where $R$ is a commutative unital ring and $M$ carries the induced boundary orientation; for $R=\mathbb F_2$ the canonical mod-two orientation may be used, so the statement applies to every compact smooth manifold. Let $i:M\hookrightarrow W$ be the inclusion and $[M]\in H_n(M;R)$ the fundamental class of the induced orientation. Then $i_*[M]=0$ in $H_n(W;R)$, and consequently $\langle i^*\alpha,[M]\rangle=0$ for every $\alpha\in H^n(W;R)$. Empty boundary, dimension zero and disconnected manifolds are included, and no AC is used.
items.strategy: Use the relative fundamental class: $\partial[W,M]=[M]$ in $H_n(M;R)$, and exactness of the homology sequence of the pair $(W,M)$ at $H_n(M;R)$, which says that the image of the connector is the kernel of $i_*$. Hence $i_*[M]=i_*\partial[W,M]=0$. Naturality of the Kronecker pairing converts the second assertion into the first.

items.title: Zero-dimensional bordism groups
items.statement:
$\Omega_0^{O}\cong\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, generated by the class of a one-point
manifold, the invariant being the parity of the cardinality of a finite set of
points; and $\Omega_0^{SO}\cong\mathbb Z$, via the isomorphism
$[M]\mapsto\sum_{x\in M}\epsilon_x$ that sends a positively oriented point to
$+1$ and a negatively oriented point to $-1$, with generator the positively
oriented point. In particular a compact zero-manifold bounds a compact
one-manifold exactly when its signed count is zero in the oriented theory, and
exactly when its cardinality is even in the unoriented theory
([[def-unoriented-and-oriented-bordism-groups]],
[[def-null-cobordant-closed-manifold]]). The proof is choice-free; it does not
use the classification of compact one-manifolds.
items.strategy: Show that parity (respectively the signed count) is a cobordism invariant by applying the boundary-pushforward lemma with $n=0$ and $R=\mathbb F_2$ (respectively $R=\mathbb Z$): the zero-th singular homology of a compact one-manifold is free on its path components, so the vanishing of $i_*[M]$ says precisely that each component receives as many positive as negative boundary points, which for $R=\mathbb F_2$ says each component receives an even number. Conversely, build an explicit bordism between any two finite point sets with equal invariant as a finite disjoint union of intervals and cylinders, using $[0,1]$ with its standard orientation for the pair of opposite signs and the cylinder for equal signs. Additivity and bijectivity follow from the explicit generators.

items.title: Product boundary formula for oriented manifolds
items.statement:
Let $W^m$ and $V^n$ be compact oriented smooth manifolds with at most one of
$\partial W,\partial V$ nonempty (the corner-free case), and give $W\times V$
its product smooth structure
([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]])
and product orientation ([[def-product-orientation]]). Then, up to a canonical
orientation-preserving diffeomorphism
([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]],
[[def-orientation-preserving-parametrization]]), the boundary
$\partial(W\times V)$ with the outward-normal-first orientation
([[def-induced-boundary-orientation]]) equals
$$(\partial W\times V)\;\sqcup\;(-1)^{m}\,(W\times\partial V),$$
each summand carrying the product orientation of the induced boundary
orientation of the factor and the supplied orientation of the other factor. In
the unoriented theory the same identity of smooth manifolds with boundary holds
without signs. If both factors are closed then $W\times V$ is closed. The case
where both boundaries are nonempty produces corners at $\partial W\times\partial
V$ and is excluded.
items.strategy: Reduce to the published product-boundary proposition, which computes the sign $(-1)^m$ by moving the outward normal of the boundary factor past the $m$ tangent directions of the other factor; restate it with the dimensions and the product-orientation convention used here. Record the excluded corner case explicitly.

items.title: Cartesian product makes bordism a graded ring
items.statement:
For both theories set $[M]\cdot[N]=[M\times N]$. This is a well-defined
biadditive associative product $\Omega_m\times\Omega_n\to\Omega_{m+n}$
distributing over disjoint union, and the class of a one-point manifold (positively oriented in the oriented theory) is a
two-sided unit. Hence $\Omega_*^{O}=\bigoplus_n\Omega_n^{O}$ is a nonnegatively
graded commutative ring ([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]],
[[def-commutative-ring]]) with unit $[\mathrm{pt}]$, and
$\Omega_*^{SO}=\bigoplus_n\Omega_n^{SO}$ carries an associative, biadditive,
unital product with the same unit
([[def-unoriented-and-oriented-bordism-groups]],
[[thm-disjoint-union-makes-bordism-classes-abelian-groups]]).

In the oriented theory the product is graded-commutative: the canonical
transposition diffeomorphism $M\times N\to N\times M$ has orientation sign
$(-1)^{mn}$ for $m=\dim M$, $n=\dim N$, so
$$[M][N]=(-1)^{mn}[N][M],$$
the Koszul sign rule; in the unoriented theory the product is commutative. The
forgetful map $\Omega_*^{SO}\to\Omega_*^{O}$ is a ring homomorphism. No choice
principle is used.
items.strategy: Well-definedness: if $W_1$ bounds $M_0$ to $M_1$ and $W_2$ bounds $N_0$ to $N_1$, restrict each to a closed factor and glue $(W_1\times N_0)\cup_{M_1\times N_0}(M_1\times W_2)$, which is corner-free because one factor of each piece is closed, using the collar-gluing lemma. Associativity and distributivity come from the canonical diffeomorphisms of products and disjoint unions; the unit is $[\mathrm{pt}]$. For graded commutativity compute the effect of the transposition on the product orientation: interchanging an $m$-block and an $n$-block costs $(-1)^{mn}$ in the determinant line.

items.title: Stiefel-Whitney numbers of a closed manifold
items.statement: Assume AC (used only through the Stiefel-Whitney class construction). Let $M$ be a closed smooth $n$-manifold, with tangent Stiefel-Whitney classes $w_i=w_i(TM)\in H^i(M;\mathbb F_2)$ and canonical mod-two fundamental class $[M]\in H_n(M;\mathbb F_2)$. For a monomial $w^{I}=w_1^{r_1}\cdots w_n^{r_n}$ with $r_1+2r_2+\cdots+nr_n=n$, the associated Stiefel-Whitney number is $w^{I}[M]=\langle w^{I},[M]\rangle\in\mathbb F_2$, the Kronecker evaluation. Monomials of total degree different from $n$ are assigned the value $0$. The Stiefel-Whitney numbers of $M$ are the values attached to all monomials of total degree $n$; they are diffeomorphism invariants and require no orientation.
items.strategy: Define the numbers by evaluating the tangent Stiefel-Whitney monomials on the canonical mod-two fundamental class, invoking the fundamental-class and Kronecker-pairing interfaces and the admissibility of closed smooth manifolds for the class construction. Check the degree convention and that no orientation is needed because the canonical mod-two orientation always exists.

items.title: Pontryagin numbers of a closed oriented manifold
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The assumption is inherited from the
Pontryagin class construction and is used only there, through
[[def-pontryagin-classes-by-complexification]] its CW-type transport below, and the admissibility supplied by
[[lem-second-countable-smooth-manifolds-have-cw-homotopy-type]].

Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth manifold of dimension $4k$ for an integer
$k\ge0$, with orientation $o$. Its **fundamental class**
$[M]\in H_{4k}(M;\mathbb Z)$ is the class determined by $o$
([[def-fundamental-class-of-a-compact-oriented-manifold]]). Its **tangent
Pontryagin classes**, taken componentwise when $M$ is disconnected, are
$$p_i \;:=\; p_i(TM)\in H^{4i}(M;\mathbb Z)\qquad(i\ge0),$$
with the conventions $p_0=1$ and $p_i=0$ whenever $2i>4k$.

**Connected case.** If $M$ is connected, then $M$ is path-connected: a manifold
is locally path-connected
([[prop-topological-manifolds-are-locally-compact-and-locally-path-connected]])
and a connected locally path-connected space is path-connected
([[thm-connected-and-locally-path-connected-implies-path-connected]]). Hence
$M$ is an admissible base for the characteristic-class construction: it is
paracompact Hausdorff of CW homotopy type and its tangent bundle is a numerable
smooth finite-rank real bundle
([[lem-second-countable-smooth-manifolds-have-cw-homotopy-type]]). For a
partition $I=(i_1,\dots,i_r)$ of $k$ with $i_j\ge1$ (for $k=0$ the empty
partition, with empty product $1$), the **$I$-th Pontryagin number** of $M$ is
$$p_I[M] \;:=\; \bigl\langle\, p_{i_1}\cdots p_{i_r},\,[M]\,\bigr\rangle \;\in\;\mathbb Z,$$
the Kronecker evaluation of the cup product of the tangent Pontryagin classes
on the fundamental class ([[def-kronecker-evaluation-pairing]]); the value is
well defined on cohomology and homology classes by
[[lem-the-kronecker-pairing-is-independent-of-cocycle-and-cycle-representatives]].

**General closed oriented manifolds.** Let $M$ be an arbitrary closed oriented
manifold of dimension $4k$. By the componentwise statement for compact
manifolds, $M$ has finitely many connected components
$M_1,\dots,M_s$; each component is open
([[prop-components-of-a-topological-manifold-are-open-and-at-most-countable]])
and closed in the compact $M$, hence compact, carries the restricted smooth
structure as an open submanifold
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]),
and carries the orientation restricted to it; the family of these restricted
orientations is the componentwise orientation of $o$
([[prop-every-manifold-is-f-two-orientable-and-orientability-is-componentwise]]).
Each $M_j$ is a closed oriented smooth $4k$-manifold and the connected case
above applies. We set
$$p_I[M] \;:=\; \sum_{j=1}^{s} p_I[M_j],$$
the sum of the componentwise Pontryagin numbers; for connected $M$ this is
exactly the single evaluation displayed above. A manifold whose dimension is
not $4|I|$ is assigned the value $0$ by convention, and $p_I[M]$ for a
partition $I$ with $i_j\ge1$ never sees a class $p_i$ of index beyond the
dimension.

The definition is independent of all choices: the complexification of $TM$ is
determined up to canonical isomorphism, so the even Chern classes, hence the
classes $p_i$, are determined; the fundamental class is determined by the
orientation; and the Kronecker pairing descends through both quotients. The
classes $p_i(TM)$ do not depend on the orientation. Replacing $o$ by $-o$
negates the fundamental class on every component
([[def-fundamental-class-of-a-compact-oriented-manifold]]) and therefore
negates every Pontryagin number, by linearity of the pairing in its second
variable ([[lem-the-kronecker-pairing-is-independent-of-cocycle-and-cycle-representatives]]).

**Naturality and stability on CW-type bases.** The cited Pontryagin theorem
is stated for path-connected CW complexes, whereas smooth manifolds here are
only known to have CW homotopy type. The needed extension is as follows.
For a numerable complex bundle $V$ over a path-connected paracompact Hausdorff
CGWH base $B$ of CW type, choose homotopy inverse maps $h:K\to B$ and
$g:B\to K$ with $K$ a path-connected CW complex. Homotopy invariance of
bundle pullback gives $V\cong g^*h^*V$
([[thm-homotopy-invariance-of-vector-bundle-pullback]]).
The Chern naturality theorem permits a CW-type source and a CW target, so
$c_j(V)=g^*c_j(h^*V)$
([[thm-naturality-normalization-and-whitney-sum-for-chern-classes]],
[[def-chern-classes-from-the-projective-bundle-relation]]).
For $f:B'\to B$ between such bases,
$f^*V\cong(g\circ f)^*h^*V$, so the same theorem with target $K$ gives
$c_j(f^*V)=f^*c_j(V)$. Also
$V\oplus\varepsilon^r\cong g^*(h^*V\oplus\varepsilon^r)$;
Chern stability on $K$ and naturality along $g$ give
$c_j(V\oplus\varepsilon^r)=c_j(V)$.
Complexification commutes with pullback and adjoining trivial summands,
as seen from their transition matrices. The formula
$p_i(E)=(-1)^ic_{2i}(E_{\mathbb C})$ therefore proves naturality and
stability of Pontryagin classes on these CW-type bases too. For a finite
disjoint union define the classes componentwise: every singular simplex lies
in one component, so cohomology is the finite product of the component rings,
with pullbacks and cup products computed componentwise. This also handles
maps whose different source components land in the same target component.
For the empty base all classes and evaluations have their unique zero values.
AC is inherited by this transport from the stated bundle-homotopy and
characteristic-class suppliers.

**Behaviour under diffeomorphisms.** Let $F:M'\to M$ be a diffeomorphism of
closed oriented $4k$-manifolds ([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]).
Assume first that $M'$ and $M$ are connected and that $F$ is
orientation-preserving ([[def-orientation-preserving-parametrization]]). The
differential of $F$ identifies $TM'$ with the pullback $F^*TM$, so naturality
of Pontryagin classes gives $p_i(TM')=F^*p_i(TM)$
(by the CW-type derivation above).
The pushforward $F_*[M']$ restricts at every $y\in M$ to the image under $dF$
of the local generator of $o'$ at $F^{-1}(y)$, which is the local generator of
$o$ at $y$ because $F$ is orientation-preserving; by the characterisation of
the fundamental class through its pointwise restrictions
([[def-fundamental-class-of-a-compact-oriented-manifold]]) this means
$F_*[M']=[M]$. Naturality of the Kronecker pairing
([[lem-the-kronecker-pairing-is-independent-of-cocycle-and-cycle-representatives]])
therefore gives
$$p_I[M']=\langle p_I(TM'),[M']\rangle=\langle F^*p_I(TM),[M']\rangle=\langle p_I(TM),F_*[M']\rangle=\langle p_I(TM),[M]\rangle=p_I[M].$$
If $F$ is orientation-reversing, the same computation gives local generators
that are negatives of those of $o$, so $F_*[M']=-[M]$ and $p_I[M']=-p_I[M]$.
For disconnected $M'$ and $M$ the argument applies to each component, and the
sum of the componentwise numbers transforms accordingly. In particular a
nonzero Pontryagin number obstructs the existence of an orientation-reversing
self-diffeomorphism. No choice beyond the AC stated above is used.
items.strategy: Define the numbers by evaluating products of Pontryagin classes on the integral fundamental class; record the degree and orientation conventions and the sign behaviour under orientation reversal, which will be used to check consistency with the boundary-vanishing proposition. Invoke admissibility of closed smooth manifolds for the class construction.

items.title: The boundary stable tangent bundle splits off a trivial line
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), used exactly through
the global inward vector field of
[[thm-every-manifold-with-boundary-has-a-global-inward-pointing-vector-field-along-the-boundary]].
Let $W$ be a smooth manifold with boundary $M=\partial W$
([[def-smooth-map-between-manifolds-with-boundary]]), let
$i:M\to W$ be the inclusion, which is a closed embedding of a smooth
$n$-manifold ([[thm-the-boundary-is-a-closed-embedded-smooth-n-minus-one-manifold]]),
and let $X$ be a smooth vector field on a neighbourhood of $M$ in $W$ that is
inward at every point of $M$
([[def-inward-outward-and-boundary-tangent-vectors]]).

Then the map
$$\Phi:TM\oplus\varepsilon^1\longrightarrow TW|_M,\qquad \Phi(v,t)=di(v)+t\,X|_M,$$
is an isomorphism of smooth real vector bundles over $M$
([[def-whitney-sum-tensor-dual-hom-and-exterior-power-bundles]],
[[def-pullback-vector-bundle-and-pullback-section]]). Consequently
$TW|_M\cong TM\oplus\varepsilon^1$ and the normal line $TW|_M/TM$ is trivial.
Since $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ supplies such an $X$ for every smooth manifold with
boundary, the splitting holds for every smooth manifold with boundary. In
particular the stabilization of $TM$ by one trivial line is identified with the
restriction $TW|_M$; this is the identification used by the characteristic
number propositions of this page.
items.strategy: Choose a smooth inward field along $M$ (published existence under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). At each boundary point the differential of the inclusion identifies $T_pM$ with the boundary-tangent hyperplane and $X(p)$ is transverse to it, so $\Phi_p$ is a linear isomorphism; smoothness in the base follows because $di$ and $X$ are smooth bundle maps, and a fibrewise-linear bijection of smooth vector bundles over the identity is a bundle isomorphism. Identify the quotient line with the trivial span of $X$. No further choice is made.

items.title: Boundaries have zero Stiefel-Whitney numbers
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), used only through the Stiefel-Whitney
class construction, its admissibility input, and the inward field used in
the boundary tangent splitting (which requires $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let $M$ be a closed smooth
$n$-manifold that is the boundary of a compact smooth $(n+1)$-manifold $W$,
with canonical mod-two fundamental class $[M]\in H_n(M;\mathbb F_2)$
([[def-stiefel-whitney-number-of-a-closed-manifold]]) and inclusion
$i:M\hookrightarrow W$. Then
$$w^{I}[M]=\langle w^{I}(TM),[M]\rangle=0$$
for every monomial $w^{I}=w_1^{r_1}\cdots w_n^{r_n}$ of total degree $n$.
Hence every Stiefel-Whitney number of a closed boundary vanishes, and a closed
manifold with at least one nonzero Stiefel-Whitney number is not
null-cobordant ([[def-null-cobordant-closed-manifold]]).
items.strategy: Restrict the tangent bundle of $W$ to $M$: naturality of Stiefel-Whitney classes gives $w(TM)=i^*w(TW)$, using the boundary splitting $TW|_M\cong TM\oplus\varepsilon^1$ and the stability of the Whitney sum formula for the trivial summand. Naturality of the Kronecker pairing gives $\langle i^*w^I(TW),[M]\rangle=\langle w^I(TW),i_*[M]\rangle$, and the fundamental class of the boundary pushes forward to zero, so the number vanishes. Note that admissibility of $M$ for the class construction holds because $M$ is a closed smooth manifold.

items.title: Oriented boundaries have zero Pontryagin numbers
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), used only through the Pontryagin class
construction, CW-type transport, admissibility input, and the inward field
used in the boundary tangent splitting (which requires $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth
$4k$-manifold that is the boundary of a compact oriented smooth
$(4k+1)$-manifold $W$, in the orientation convention of the null-cobordism
definition ([[def-null-cobordant-closed-manifold]]), with fundamental class
$[M]\in H_{4k}(M;\mathbb Z)$ and inclusion $i:M\hookrightarrow W$. Then
$$p_I[M]=\langle p_{i_1}\cdots p_{i_r},[M]\rangle=0$$
for every partition $I=(i_1,\dots,i_r)$ of $k$. Hence a closed oriented
$4k$-manifold with a nonzero Pontryagin number is not an oriented boundary.
The proof uses neither the signature nor the Hirzebruch signature theorem.
items.strategy: Restrict the Pontryagin classes to $M$: naturality and stability of Pontryagin classes under adjoining a trivial line give $p(TM)=i^*p(TW)$ using the boundary splitting $TW|_M\cong TM\oplus\varepsilon^1$. Naturality of the integral Kronecker pairing and the boundary-pushforward lemma turn the number into $\langle p_I(TW),i_*[M]\rangle=0$.

items.title: Bordism groups here are geometric, not generalized homology constructions
items.statement: The groups $\Omega_n^{O}$ and $\Omega_n^{SO}$ defined on this page are geometric: their elements are bordism classes of manifolds and their operation is disjoint union, with products given by Cartesian product. This page constructs no Thom spectrum, no ring spectrum, and no generalized homology theory; the identification of these groups with stable homotopy groups of Thom spectra (for instance $\Omega_n^{O}\cong\pi_n(MO)$ and $\Omega_n^{SO}\cong\pi_n(MSO)$), together with the Thom transversality theorem and the bordism homology axioms, belongs to algebraic topology and to later pages. The remark fixes the seam so that consumers do not read a spectrum-level claim into these definitions.
items.strategy: Record the boundary between the geometric definitions of this page and the Thom-spectrum constructions of algebraic topology; cite the sources for the identification as the destination of that material without asserting it here.

title: Smooth Cobordism Relations Groups and Rings — Examples

items.title: A circle is the boundary of a disk
items.statement: The closed unit disk $D^2=\overline B_2(0,1)\subset\mathbb R^2$ is a compact smooth surface with boundary $S^1$; with the orientation of $D^2$ induced from the standard orientation of $\mathbb R^2$, its induced boundary orientation is the standard counterclockwise orientation of $S^1$. Consequently $S^1$ with that orientation is null-cobordant, so its class is zero in $\Omega_1^{SO}$ and in $\Omega_1^{O}$; the circle with the opposite orientation is the inverse of $S^1$ in $\Omega_1^{SO}$.
items.strategy: Construct $D^2$ as a smooth manifold with boundary using boundary-defining-function charts ($\rho(x)=1-|x|^2$ with nonzero gradient on $S^1$) and the inverse function theorem, as in the published closed-ball example; compute the outward normal at $p\in S^1$ as the radial direction and verify that outward-normal-first on $\partial D^2$ is counterclockwise. Identify the resulting bordism from $S^1$ to the empty 1-manifold and read off null-cobordism.

items.title: Two unoriented points bound an interval
items.statement: The closed interval $[-1,1]$ is a compact smooth one-manifold with boundary $\{-1,1\}$; hence the disjoint union of two points, as a closed zero-manifold, is null-cobordant and $[\mathrm{pt}]+[\mathrm{pt}]=0$ in $\Omega_0^{O}$. Since a single point is not null-cobordant (its parity is odd), the class of the one-point manifold is the unique nonzero element of $\Omega_0^{O}\cong\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. Thus every closed zero-manifold with an even number of points is null-cobordant.
items.strategy: Exhibit the interval as a compact smooth one-manifold with boundary via the closed-ball model in $\mathbb R^1$, compute that its two boundary points form a null-cobordant zero-manifold, and combine with the parity invariant of the zero-dimensional proposition to conclude that the point class is nonzero and self-inverse.

items.title: Signed points give the oriented zero-bordism invariant
items.statement: For a closed oriented zero-manifold $M=\coprod_{x}\{x\}$ with signs $\epsilon_x\in\{\pm1\}$ determined by the orientation, the integer $\sum_{x}\epsilon_x$ is unchanged by oriented cobordism, and the map $[M]\mapsto\sum_x\epsilon_x$ is an isomorphism $\Omega_0^{SO}\to\mathbb Z$. A positively oriented point is a generator, and the standard interval $[-1,1]$ realizes $[\mathrm{pt}_+]+[\mathrm{pt}_-]=0$ with the sign convention of the page, so $[\mathrm{pt}_-]=-[\mathrm{pt}_+]$. Consequently two finite oriented point sets are oriented cobordant exactly when their signed counts agree.
items.strategy: Verify the invariant by exhibiting the oriented interval as a null-cobordism of one positive and one negative point and by additivity of the signed count under disjoint union; bijectivity follows from the explicit generator and the computation of the inverse. Use the product boundary orientation to fix the signs of the interval ends.

items.title: The pair of pants is a cobordism realizing addition of circles
items.statement: Let $P=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:\|(x,y)\|\le2,\ \|(x,y)-(1,0)\|\ge1,\ \|(x,y)+(1,0)\|\ge1\}$, the disk of radius $2$ with two disjoint open unit disks removed. Then $P$ is a compact oriented smooth surface with boundary three circles, and with the outward-normal-first orientation its boundary is $-(S^1_1\sqcup S^1_2)\sqcup S^1_3$ for a suitable pairing of the three boundary circles into incoming and outgoing parts (the labels depend on the chosen decomposition, and the reversed decomposition gives the same bordism read backwards). Hence $P$ is a bordism from two circles to one circle and exhibits in $\Omega_1^{SO}$ the additive relation $[S^1_1]+[S^1_2]=[S^1_3]$; all three classes are zero by the preceding example, so the example illustrates disjoint-union addition rather than an independent invariant.
items.strategy: Give $P$ its smooth structure as a regular region in the plane: each boundary point lies on exactly one of the three circles, where the defining function is smooth with nonzero gradient, so the closed-ball chart construction applies and $P$ is a compact manifold with boundary with boundary the three circles. Compute the induced boundary orientation of each circle (outer circle counterclockwise, the two inner circles clockwise for the standard plane orientation) and split the boundary into incoming and outgoing parts so that the oriented boundary is $-(S^1_1\sqcup S^1_2)\sqcup S^1_3$. Compactness follows from closedness in the compact disk of radius $2$.

items.title: The real projective plane is not unoriented null-cobordant
items.statement:
It is false that the real projective plane is null-cobordant: there is no
compact smooth $3$-manifold whose boundary is $\mathbb{RP}^2$, so not every
closed surface bounds. The counterexample computes the Stiefel-Whitney number
$$w_1^{2}[\mathbb{RP}^2]=\langle w_1(T\mathbb{RP}^2)^2,[\mathbb{RP}^2]\rangle=1$$
and concludes that the class of $\mathbb{RP}^2$ is a nonzero element of
$\Omega_2^{O}$ ([[def-unoriented-and-oriented-bordism-groups]]).
items.strategy: Model $\mathbb{RP}^2$ as the projectivization of the trivial rank-three real bundle over a point; the projective-bundle theorem then gives $H^*(\mathbb{RP}^2;\mathbb F_2)=\mathbb F_2[x]/(x^3)$ with $x\ne0$ in degree one. Admissibility of $\mathbb{RP}^2$ for the class construction follows from its published finite CW structure, and its smooth tangent bundle is numerable by the admissibility lemma for smooth manifolds. Non-orientability of $\mathbb{RP}^2$ and the classification of orientability by $w_1$ give $w_1(T\mathbb{RP}^2)\ne0$, hence $w_1=x$. Poincare duality over the field $\mathbb F_2$ makes the cup pairing $H^1\times H^1\to H^2$, $\langle a\smile b,[\mathbb{RP}^2]\rangle$, nonsingular, so the evaluation $\langle x^2,[\mathbb{RP}^2]\rangle$ is $1$ and the Stiefel-Whitney number is nonzero. Then invoke the boundary-vanishing proposition.
